****************************************************************************\nvoid fill(double* A, const index_t n, const double maxVal) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i] = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initRandomMatrix\n//\n// Purpose:\n// - ((i * dim) + j);\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\n                fillRemaining = true;\n            }\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                cols[nnzAssigned] rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// For the vector x, since column indices can point anywhere, I'll generate it fully on rank 0 and broadcast it to every rank rather than trying to distribute it.\n\nSince each iteration recomputes the same spmv with an unchanged vec, the results are identical across iterations, so I just need to keep running the same number of iterations for timing fidelity, with row-distributed output gathered to rank 0 only when printing or validating.\n\nI'll keep each iteration doing a local SpMV with no extra per-iteration communication, since x stays constant. I'll add a barrier before timing starts and reduce timings across ranks with a max to capture the slowest rank, keep the gflops/time reporting format similar to the original, and use the same timing mechanism for consistency.\n\nFor output gathering, I'll use MPI_Gatherv to collect the full result vector on rank 0 so print_results can compute the same Kahan sum and hash as before. For validation, I'm considering having rank 0 retain a full copy of the matrix from generation so it can compute the serial reference independently and compare against the gathered result.\n\nActually, a simpler, more memory-scalable approach: compute the reference per-rank using spmvCpu on each rank's own local block before the timing loop, compare locally, then combine pass/fail across ranks with MPI_Allreduce using logical AND. That avoids needing the full matrix anywhere and mirrors the original's logic of comparing the same algorithm against itself.\n\nFor the error message, I need to adjust verifyResults to accept an offset so it reports the correct global row index rather than the local one. For generation, instead of materializing the full matrix on rank 0 and holding it in memory, it's better to generate row blocks incrementally and scatter them to owners as they're produced, avoiding storing the entire matrix at once.\n\nBut the real bottleneck remains: the generator is inherently sequential, so even a streaming approach still requires O(n^2) random draws serially on rank 0, making generation itself slow regardless of memory handling — unless the matrix semantics can be changed, which isn't an option here.\n\nWith n=1024, that's about 1M random calls, roughly 20ms—negligible. I'm settling on each rank running an identical deterministic generator with a fixed seed, storing only its own row range: no communication needed, memory stays local, though compute is redundantly repeated across ranks but in parallel so wall-time matches serial. The tricky part is that filling val requires generating values in strict index order through the entire nItems stream, since values are tied to nnz position.\n\nEach rank must advance through the full random sequence—generating vec's numRows rands, then val's nItems rands—even though it only stores its local slice, discarding the rest since it's cheap. The harder issue is mapping which nnz entries belong to which row: row delimiters from the matrix generator define nnz ranges per row, so a rank can track nnzAssigned as it streams through rows and only store columns falling in its local range, avoiding full-array storage of cols and values which would blow up per-rank memory and defeat the whole distribution approach.\n\nOnce fillRemaining triggers, assignments happen unconditionally and total hits exactly n, so no overflow concern there. I should keep the dim*dim arithmetic in uint32 identical to the original for equivalence, even though it could overflow for very large dim — that's existing behavior I shouldn't change. Since we can break early after processing row r1, the subsequent rand calls don't affect the matrix output, so skipping them should be safe.\n\nThe per-row generation cost is O(dim) regardless of whether a rank actually keeps those rows, so for large n this init work scales as O(n²) serially per rank — expensive, but equivalent to the original's single-threaded cost, so wall time doesn't get worse. A centralized generate-on-rank-0-then-scatter approach would have the same serial bottleneck, so the redundant per-rank generation with zero communication is just as good and simpler, worth flagging in the summary.\n\nI'm also noting that since glibc's rand has no skip-ahead, every rank must generate the full vec and val sequences in order to land on the right stream position, discarding non-local values without storing them — meaning the local val slice can only be known after computing local nnz ranges from the matrix generator itself, which happens after the srand reset.\n\nActually the order matters: the original generates the val stream first using the untouched default state, then calls srand(8675309) for the matrix structure. So I should preserve that exact sequence rather than reordering it.\n\nConfirmed by the C standard that rand's default seed is 1, so an explicit srand(1) is conforming. But I'm second-guessing the scalable streaming approach — a simpler alternative would be each rank generating the full val/vec/matrix arrays temporarily, though that costs O(nnz) memory per rank and won't scale for huge matrices, so I'd rather stick with the scalable method despite its complexity.\n\nWorking through the structure: each rank sets srand(8675309), runs the matrix generator restricted to its local row range to get local columns and relative row delimiters, plus the global nnz offsets marking where its slice starts and ends. Then it reseeds with srand(1), fills the full vec array (since all ranks need it), and iterates through all nItems rand calls for val, keeping only the values that fall within its local nnz range — careful to preserve the fill order of vec before val to match the original generator's sequence.\n\nI'm also handling edge cases: ranks with zero assigned rows skip matrix generation entirely since r0 equals r1, and the nnz offsets k0 and k1 are captured at the start of row r0 and the end of row r1-1 respectively.\n\nFor capturing local entries, I'll push matched column values into a local buffer as rows are iterated, and build the local row delimiter array offset from nnzAssigned - k0, mirroring how the original sets rowDelimiters[dim] = n but scoped to just this rank's slice.\n\nFor the distributed SpMV, each rank now holds its local values, local column indices (still global), its own row delimiters, and the full replicated vector, so I can reuse spmvCpu directly per iteration since the row delimiters are already relative to the local array—no need to rewrite the kernel. I'm noting that the generator's dim*dim sizing needs to stay consistent with index_t semantics to avoid overflow, and that performance-wise spmvCpu is still the naive loop, so there's room to optimize the inner loop later if needed.\n\nI'm weighing whether to add OpenMP for hybrid parallelism, but since the task centers on MPI and avoiding extra dependencies, I'll skip that and stay focused. I'm also considering whether to balance row partitioning by nnz rather than by row count for better load balance, but since each rank already runs the full generator redundantly, computing the full row delimiters first would require either a second generator pass or storing the full array of row boundaries, which is cheap in memory but doubles init cost — I'm weighing whether that tradeoff is worth it.\n\nFor simplicity I'll just split rows evenly across ranks, since for uniformly random sparsity this approximates balanced nnz well enough, and the replicated vector only costs O(dim) per rank with no per-iteration communication needed. For timing, I'll bracket the compute loop with MPI_Barrier calls, measure elapsed time per rank with chrono, then reduce with MPI_Reduce using MAX to get the slowest rank's time, converting that to milliseconds for the printed output while keeping the original Gflops formula based on total work divided by elapsed time. For output and validation, local comparisons don't need communication, but printing the full result vector requires gathering each rank's local output into rank 0 via MPI_Gatherv with proper counts and displacements, which I'll only do when results need to be printed rather than just validated.\n\nI need to make verifyResults account for a global index offset so failure messages report the correct global index rather than a local one, and combine per-rank pass/fail status across ranks using MPI_Allreduce with a logical AND so all ranks agree on the final validation outcome and return a consistent exit code. Edge cases like `-n 0` causing division-by-zero in the sparsity percentage calculation already existed in the original code, so I'll leave that behavior unchanged rather than trying to fix it.\n\nFor the data layout, each rank keeps a replicated copy of the full vector while working on local matrix rows, and I'm keeping the CPU SpMV kernel largely as-is since the compiler handles vectorization reasonably with -march=native enabled. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793125554572,"sessionID":"ses_e81652300ffe2v6a7S5MFuRVKS","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01UxohfFzk8ZHh7nCNUvWAA9","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r5/spmv/spmv.cpp","content":"#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nusing index_t = uint32_t;\n\n// Constants\nconstexpr double MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR = 0.02;\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: fill\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Initialize array with random values\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   A: pointer to the array to initialize\n//   n: number of elements in the array\n//   maxVal: specifies range of random values [0, maxVal]\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid fill(double* A, const index_t n, const double maxVal) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i] = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Struct: LocalMatrix\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   The contiguous block of CSR rows owned by one MPI rank. Column indices\n//   are global; row delimiters are relative to the first local nonzero.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nstruct LocalMatrix {\n    index_t rowBegin = 0;   // first global row owned by this rank\n    index_t rowEnd = 0;     // one past the last global row owned by this rank\n    index_t nnzBegin = 0;   // global index of the first local nonzero\n    std::vector<double> val;                // local non-zero values\n    std::vector<index_t> cols;              // local column indices\n    std::vector<index_t> rowDelimiters;     // size rows()+1, relative to nnzBegin\n\n    index_t rows() const { return rowEnd - rowBegin; }\n};\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: partitionRows\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Block-distributes dim rows over size ranks. Blocks differ in size by at\n//   most one row.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid partitionRows(const index_t dim, const int rank, const int size,\n                   index_t& begin, index_t& end) {\n    const uint64_t d = dim;\n    begin = static_cast<index_t>(d * static_cast<uint64_t>(rank) / static_cast<uint64_t>(size));\n    end = static_cast<index_t>(d * static_cast<uint64_t>(rank + 1) / static_cast<uint64_t>(size));\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initLocalMatrix\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Regenerates the same random sparsity pattern as the serial generator\n//   (identical RNG call sequence), but materializes only the rows in\n//   [m.rowBegin, m.rowEnd). The generator is inherently sequential, so every\n//   rank replays it and keeps its own block; no communication is required and\n//   per-rank memory scales with the local share of the matrix.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   m:    receives the local rows (rowBegin/rowEnd must be set by the caller)\n//   n:    total number of nonzero elements\n//   dim:  number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid initLocalMatrix(LocalMatrix& m, const index_t n, const index_t dim) {\n    const index_t localRows = m.rows();\n    m.nnzBegin = 0;\n    m.cols.clear();\n    m.rowDelimiters.assign(localRows + 1, 0);\n    if (localRows == 0) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // Figure out the probability that a nonzero should be assigned\n    const double prob = static_cast<double>(n) / (static_cast<double>(dim) * static_cast<double>(dim));\n\n    // Seed random number generator (same seed as the serial version)\n    srand(8675309);\n\n    index_t nnzAssigned = 0;\n    // Randomly decide whether entry i,j gets a value, but ensure n values are assigned\n    bool fillRemaining = false;\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < m.rowEnd; ++i) {\n        const bool local = (i >= m.rowBegin);\n        if (i == m.rowBegin) {\n            m.nnzBegin = nnzAssigned;\n        }\n        if (local) {\n            m.rowDelimiters[i - m.rowBegin] = nnzAssigned - m.nnzBegin;\n        }\n        for (index_t j = 0; j < dim; ++j) {\n            index_t numEntriesLeft = (dim * dim) - ((i * dim) + j);\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\n                fillRemaining = true;\n            }\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                if (local) {\n                    m.cols.push_back(j);\n                }\n                nnzAssigned++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    // Convention: the number of local non-zeroes ends the local row delimiters\n    m.rowDelimiters[localRows] = nnzAssigned - m.nnzBegin;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initLocalData\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Builds this rank's matrix block and the full dense vector. Random values\n//   are drawn in the same order as the serial program (vector first, then the\n//   non-zero values, with the matrix pattern generated from its own seed), so\n//   the data is bit-identical to the serial version. Only the local slice of\n//   the non-zero values is stored.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid initLocalData(LocalMatrix& m, std::vector<double>& vec,\n                   const index_t n, const index_t dim, const double maxVal) {\n    initLocalMatrix(m, n, dim);\n\n    // The serial program draws the vector and values from the default RNG\n    // state (equivalent to seed 1) before the matrix generator reseeds.\n    srand(1);\n    vec.resize(dim);\n    fill(vec.data(), dim, maxVal);\n\n    const index_t localNnz = static_cast<index_t>(m.cols.size());\n    m.val.resize(localNnz);\n    // Consume the full value stream, storing only the local slice\n    for (index_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n        const double v = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n        if (k >= m.nnzBegin && k - m.nnzBegin < localNnz) {\n            m.val[k - m.nnzBegin] = v;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvCpu\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Computes sparse matrix-vector multiplication using CSR format\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val: array holding the non-zero values for the matrix\n//   cols: array of column indices for each element\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   vec: dense vector of size dim to be used for multiplication\n//   dim: number of rows in the (local) matrix\n//   out: output - result from the spmv calculation\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* __restrict val, const index_t* __restrict cols,\n             const index_t* __restrict rowDelimiters, const double* __restrict vec,\n             const index_t dim, double* __restrict out) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: verifyResults\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Verifies correctness of results by comparing to reference solution\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   reference: array holding the reference result vector\n//   result: array holding the result vector to verify\n//   size: number of elements per vector\n//   offset: global index of element 0 (for diagnostics)\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nbool verifyResults(const double* reference, const double* result, const index_t size,\n                   const index_t offset) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < size; ++i) {\n        const double ref = reference[i];\n        const double res = result[i];\n        if (std::abs(ref) < 1e-10) {\n            // For very small values, check absolute error\n            if (std::abs(res) > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e\\n\", offset + i, ref, res);\n                return false;\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Check relative error\n            const double relError = std::abs((res - ref) / ref);\n            if (relError > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e (rel error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       offset + i, ref, res, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of rows/columns in the matrix (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -s <num>     Sparsity: 1 out of N entries is non-zero (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of iterations (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -m <val>     Maximum value for matrix and vector elements (default: 1.0)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    index_t numRows = 1024;\n    index_t sparsity = 10;\n    index_t iterations = 10;\n    double maxVal = 1.0;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments (identical on every rank)\n    int exitCode = -1;  // -1: continue running the benchmark\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numRows = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-s\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            sparsity = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-m\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            maxVal = atof(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            exitCode = 0;\n            break;\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            exitCode = 1;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if (exitCode >= 0) {\n        MPI_Finalize();\n        return exitCode;\n    }\n\n    // Calculate number of non-zero elements\n    const index_t nItems = (numRows * numRows) / sparsity;\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SpMV) Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %u x %u\\n\", numRows, numRows);\n        printf(\"Sparsity: 1 out of %u entries is non-zero\\n\", sparsity);\n        printf(\"Non-zero elements: %u (%.2f%% sparse)\\n\", \n               nItems, 100.0 * (1.0 - static_cast<double>(nItems) / (numRows * numRows)));\n        printf(\"Iterations: %u\\n\", iterations);\n        printf(\"Max value: %.2f\\n\", maxVal);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n        printf(\"MPI ranks: %d\\n\", size);\n        printf(\"Initializing data structures...\\n\");\n    }\n\n    // Each rank owns a contiguous block of rows\n    LocalMatrix mat;\n    partitionRows(numRows, rank, size, mat.rowBegin, mat.rowEnd);\n    const index_t localRows = mat.rows();\n\n    std::vector<double> h_vec;  // Dense vector, replicated on every rank\n    initLocalData(mat, h_vec, nItems, numRows, maxVal);\n\n    std::vector<double> h_out(localRows);  // Local slice of the output vector\n\n    // For validation, compute the reference solution for the local rows\n    std::vector<double> h_reference;\n    if (validate) {\n        if (root) printf(\"Computing reference solution...\\n\");\n        h_reference.resize(localRows);\n        spmvCpu(mat.val.data(), mat.cols.data(), mat.rowDelimiters.data(),\n                h_vec.data(), localRows, h_reference.data());\n    }\n\n    // Perform SpMV computation\n    if (root) printf(\"Computing SpMV...\\n\");\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    for (index_t iter = 0; iter < iterations; ++iter) {\n        spmvCpu(mat.val.data(), mat.cols.data(), mat.rowDelimiters.data(),\n                h_vec.data(), localRows, h_out.data());\n    }\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    // The slowest rank determines the wall time of the parallel computation\n    const double localSec = std::chrono::duration<double>(end - start).count();\n    double slowestSec = 0.0;\n    MPI_Reduce(&localSec, &slowestSec, 1, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n    if (root) {\n        const auto durationMs = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(\n            std::chrono::duration<double>(slowestSec));\n        printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", static_cast<long>(durationMs.count()));\n\n        // Calculate performance metrics\n        const double gflops = (2.0 * nItems * iterations) / slowestSec / 1e9;\n        const double avgTime = (slowestSec * 1000.0) / static_cast<double>(iterations);\n\n        printf(\"Average time per iteration: %.3f ms\\n\", avgTime);\n        printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    }\n\n    // Print results for external validation (gather the full output vector)\n    if (printResults) {\n        std::vector<int> counts(size);\n        std::vector<int> displs(size);\n        for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n            index_t b = 0;\n            index_t e = 0;\n            partitionRows(numRows, r, size, b, e);\n            counts[r] = static_cast<int>(e - b);\n            displs[r] = static_cast<int>(b);\n        }\n        std::vector<double> fullOut(root ? numRows : 0);\n        MPI_Gatherv(h_out.data(), static_cast<int>(localRows), MPI_DOUBLE,\n                    fullOut.data(), counts.data(), displs.data(), MPI_DOUBLE, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        if (root) {\n            print_results(fullOut, \"OutputVector\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    int exitStatus = 0;\n    if (validate) {\n        if (root) printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        const bool localValid = verifyResults(h_reference.data(), h_out.data(), localRows, mat.rowBegin);\n        int localOk = localValid ? 1 : 0;\n        int allOk = 0;\n        MPI_Allreduce(&localOk, &allOk, 1, MPI_INT, MPI_LAND, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        const bool valid = (allOk != 0);\n\n        if (root) {\n            printf(valid ? \"Validation: PASSED\\n\" : \"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n        }\n        exitStatus = valid ? 0 : 1;\n    }\n\n    MPI_Finalize();\n    return exitStatus;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file
